title: Pocket trial grid: latency vs quantization (personal)
content:
Purpose: tiny personal tracker for quick-ish A/Bs across quantization modes and batching. Use this when I need a fast 'is q4_0 worthwhile at 512 seq' sanity check before putting larger runs in CI.

Legend: q=quantization mode, bs=batch size, seq=sequence length used (tokens), tps=tokens/sec measured from local harness, p50/p95 in ms for first-token (approx), est_cost = back-of-envelope cost per 1k tokens (GPU-min pricing estimate).

Table (rows are individual short runs; not exhaustive):

run_id, model, q, bs, seq, tps, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_generated, wall_time_s, est_cost_per_1k_tokens, notes
r001, llm-base-30b, fp16, 1, 128, 950, 90, 240, 12800, 13.5, $0.065, baseline host-run on g4-like env (no cache)
r002, llm-base-30b, q4_0, 1, 128, 1200, 80, 190, 12800, 10.7, $0.048, q4_0 reduced mem, small latency improvement
r003, llm-base-30b, q4_0, 4, 128, 4200, 75, 170, 51200, 12.1, $0.012, batching helps throughput; p95 still OK
r004, llm-base-30b, q8_0, 1, 128, 2000, 70, 160, 12800, 6.4, $0.040, q8 gives better tps vs q4_0 but memory tradeoff
r005, llama-mini-7b, q4_0, 1, 512, 1300, 140, 360, 51200, 39.4, $0.020, long seq penalizes p50; consider KV cache
r006, llama-mini-7b, q4_0, 8, 512, 9000, 130, 310, 409600, 45.5, $0.004, high batch efficiency but memory bound occasionally
r007, llm-base-30b, q4_0+kvcache, 1, 1024, 1100, 160, 420, 112640, 102.4, $0.010, KV cache warming -- first run slower; subsequent runs ~= r002 tps
r008, llm-base-30b, fp16, 2, 256, 1800, 85, 200, 25600, 14.2, $0.060, small batch -> good lat/throughput balance

Quick observations:
- q4_0 consistently saves cost and gives modest latency improvement vs fp16 at low bs; q8_0 gives higher tps but sometimes worse p95.
- Batching (bs >=4) increases aggregate tps but adds tail latency; for user-facing SLOs prefer bs 1-2 unless background jobs.
- Large seq (512+) drastically increases p50/p95; KV cache is high leverage if prompt prefixes repeat.
- Estimate formula used: est_cost_per_1k_tokens = (gpu_price_per_hour * wall_time_s/3600) / (tokens_generated/1000). Using gpu_price_per_hour = $2.5 for quick local approximations.

Notes / TODOs:
- Re-run r003 with q4_0 + async batching (slotting) to check p95 improvement (ticket JIRA-MLINF-421).
- Add a small memory column next time (GPU RAM used) — current harness didn't capture OOM thresholds.
- Capture cold vs warm KV cache numbers (r007 suggests big warm gap).
- Try mixed precision + dynamic batching (1-4) for latency-sensitive route.
- Save promising configs to dedicated mini-suite for CI: r002 (q4_0 bs1 128), r004 (q8_0 bs1 128), r006 (7b q4_0 bs8 512).

Short mental checklist when doing quick runs:
- note rig (GPU type, driver)
- clear cache between runs unless testing warm state
- set deterministic sampler for regen consistency
- record seed + prompt length

Scratch calcs (working):
- r002 wall_time_s = tokens_generated / tps = 12800 / 1200 ~= 10.67s (matches measured 10.7)
- est_cost_per_1k = (2.5 * 10.7/3600)/(12.8) = ~0.048 -> used above

Freeform log (short):
- 2026-02-20: noticed weird p95 jump on r004 after system update; likely cudnn kernel change. Reboot + pinned driver restored earlier numbers.
- 2026-02-23: consolidated small runs into this pocket tracker. Will push winning short-configs to infra-suites next week.

End of sheet. Will keep terse — meant for very fast triage rather than repeatable record. Move to 'suites/mini-ci' only after 3 consistent runs across rigs.
